[[File:EmperorsSkyhook-SOTETC.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]] admires the Botanical gardens on the [[Emperor's skyhook]].]]
'''Skyhooks''', or '''spacehooks''', were [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsor]] craft that floated above the surface of a [[Planet/Legends|planet]], but remained within its [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]].<ref name="CNII">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]'', 16</ref> They were commonly symbols of status among the very wealthy, and were usually found on heavily populated worlds, such as [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].

==Technology==
Skyhooks were sometimes tethered by [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] nanofibers.<ref name="CNII" />

Sometimes massive moorings were constructed on the surface of the planet, typically by [[metal/Legends|metal]], [[permacrete/Legends|permacrete]], and stone; their interior contained more delicate systems such as hydraulic channels, nanowires, and other mechanics that would regulate themselves with high sensitivity.<ref name="TFU" />

==History==
Under the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], skyhooks were at one point banned due to the possibility of system failures which would send them crashing into the Coruscant surface. This fear was based on a rare occurrence, a combination of a lightning storm and a freak accident. Such accidents were only known to occur around once every century. Under the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the skyhook ban was dropped.

[[Core Worlds Engineering/Legends|Core Worlds Engineering]] was known to manufacture skyhooks.

After its conquest of Coruscant in [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]], the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] made no moves to reinstate the ban. However, when the [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]] ''[[Lusankya/Legends|Lusankya]]'' broke free from its berth under the planet's surface, she fired on a skyhook, destroying it and causing its remains to crash into the planet's surface, damaging several square kilometers of the cityscape.

In the aftermath of the massive ship's departure, the [[New Republic Provisional Council]] ordered the grounding of all skyhooks in the area of the city destroyed by the ship. Though a popular rumor stated that the Council had ordered the skyhooks down in order to spite former members of [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]], the Council officially stated that its aim was to provide shelter to those who had had their homes destroyed in the ''Lusankya''s escape.<ref name="The Bacta War">''[[X-Wing: The Bacta War]]''</ref>

By the time of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], skyhooks were again a common sight in Coruscant. Following the [[Battle of Coruscant (Yuuzhan Vong War)|Battle of Coruscant]], the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] tore a number of them out of orbit, causing them to crash to the planet's surface, each impact killing millions and devastating hundreds of kilometers of cityscape.<ref name="NJO">''[[The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines I: Rebel Dream]]''</ref>

==Examples==
On [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], the Empire was constructing a [[Skyhook (Kashyyyk)|skyhook]] to ferry [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] to low orbit to be transported to labor camps across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], under the supervision of [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Ozzik Sturn]]. But [[Galen Marek]] destroyed the mooring points that kept the skyhook stable, causing it to blow up. This gave the Wookiees some time to go into hiding, even if, as Marek thought, a replacement would be built sooner or later.<ref name="TFU">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref>

[[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] possessed a [[Emperor's skyhook|lavish skyhook]] in which he housed his greatest treasures, preferring to keep the most priceless ones in the air instead of in his [[Imperial Palace/Legends|palace]]. The botanist in charge of his orbiting garden was one of the best in the galaxy. When Prince Xizor attempted to hire him away from the Emperor's service, the botanist was killed in a mysterious elevator 'accident', which no doubt occurred under the direction of Palpatine.

[[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]], leader of the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] criminal organization, also had his own skyhook above [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], a [[Core Worlds Engineering/Legends|Core Worlds Engineering]] [[Skyhook Platform]] which was known as ''[[Falleen's Fist]]''.<ref name="SotES">''[[Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> It was destroyed by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] when he commanded the [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']] to fire at it during the [[Battle over Coruscant]]. Xizor was killed when the skyhook was destroyed.

[[File:HB_SotE_skyhook_death.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The [[Falleen's Fist]] is destroyed by the [[Executor/Legends|Executor]].]]
There were a number of other skyhooks operating on Coruscant, including one owned by Vader himself. One of these was the [[SoroSuub Corporation/Legends|SoroSuub]] skyhook, which was offered to the former members of Rogue Squadron before the Council ordered the grounding of all skyhooks.

The economic powerhouse of [[Muunilinst/Legends|Muunilinst]] had a skyhook connecting the orbital city of [[High Port Space Center|High Port]] with the capital [[Harnaidan]], the skyhook tethered the station in place and allowed for cheap travel up and from the planet's surface.

==Behind the scenes==
In science fiction, [[Wikipedia:Skyhook (structure)|skyhooks]] are hypothetical structures used for transporting material to and from a planet's surface into orbit, continuously supporting it rather than using rockets, catapults, or hypothetical anti-gravity effects. The term was coined by scientist Giuseppe Colombo.

In real life, it is an object that connects earth vertically with sky; for example, atmospheric research balloons, types of helicopters, etc. It is not clear which concept preceded which.
